name: lemma22_affine_kernel
doc:
Lemma 2.2 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:657-659` (label `lemma:linear-lie-in-kernel`): for every
`p ∈ ℝ^d` and `c ∈ ℝ`, the affine function `ℓ_p(x) = p ⬝ x + c` satisfies `Δ_a ℓ_p = 0`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Correction 4): at every vertex whose cell is
complete (finitely many neighbours, and every boundary point of the cell lies in the cell of a
neighbour).  The published identity is false at a cell with a facet shared with no other cell (two
unit squares: `ℓ(x) = x₁` has discrete Laplacian `1` at the left square).  Proved from leobon12's
polytope Gauss–Green identity.

name: lemma23_dual_variational
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.FiniteConductanceNetwork SpherePackings
open scoped BigOperators

open Classical in
doc:
Lemma 2.3 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:684-690` (label `lemma:dual-variational-principle`): for a finite
set `A`, `f` zero on `∂A` and a vector field `θ` on `E[Ā]` with `div θ = div(∇_a f)` on `A`,
`∑_{e ∈ E[Ā]} a(e)⁻¹ |∇_a f(e)|² ≤ ∑_{e ∈ E[Ā]} a(e)⁻¹ θ(e)²`.

Stated for a finite network with arbitrary symmetric nonnegative conductances (the tiling
conductances on a finite set of vertices are one); `E[Ā]` is the set of directed edges of positive
conductance with an endpoint in `A`, and `θ` vanishes off it.  Proved from leobon12's dual
variational lemmas.

name: lemma24_dual_volume

doc:
Lemma 2.4 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:739-744` (label `lemma:geometry-bound`): for each edge
`e = (w, v)`, `‖w - v‖ vol_{d-1}(H_e) = d vol_d(Q_e)`, where `Q_e = conv(w, H_e) ∪ conv(v, H_e)`.

leobon12's theorem; `dualVolume` is the volume of `dualPolytope v w`, the union of the two
pyramids over the contact.

name: lemma31_poincare
opens:
open scoped Classical BigOperators MeasureTheory ENNReal
open MeasureTheory BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
doc:
Lemma 3.1 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:937-943` (label `lemma:ptype-inequality`): for `f` zero on
`∂V[U]`, the `(d-1)`-volume of the set of `y ∈ π_j(U)` with
`max_{v ∈ L_y^j[U]} |f(v)| > k (D(f, U) ∑_{e ∈ E[Ū]} d vol_d(Q_e))^{1/2}` is at most `1/k`.

On a finite set `R` of vertices containing the neighbours of `A`: columns in any direction `e ≠ 0`;
the bad set is the set of `y` in the projection of the cell of a vertex of `A` with `|f| > τ`;
`incidentEnergy` is `D(f, U)` and `incidentMass` is `∑ ‖e‖ vol_{d-1}(H_e)`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Correction 4): the cells of `A` are complete.  The
published lemma is false without it: for two unit squares in a row and `U` containing both
centres, `∂V[U]` is empty, and `f = 1` has `D(f, U) = 0` while the bad set at threshold `0` is
`π_1(U)`, of positive length.  Proved from leobon12's column lemmas, adapted to complete cells.

name: theorem33_planar
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
open scoped MeasureTheory Laplacian
doc:
Theorem 3.3 of rw-spheres.tex, the bound, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1030-1049` (label `theorem:2d`): in the plane,
`sup_{V[U]} |h_D - h_C| ≤ inf_{k > 0} (6 k M ε vol(Û) + 2 (√2 k⁻¹ + ε) L)`, with
`ε = sup_{V̄[U]} diam(P_v)`, `L = sup_Û |∇ h_C|`, `M = sup_Û |∇² h_C|`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4 and 8 and the revised Theorem 3.3,
corrections items 1, 5 and 6): `sup_{V[U]} |h_D - h_C| ≤ 3 M₀ ε² + inf_{k > 0} (6 k M ε vol(Û) +
(M/2)(√2 k⁻¹ + ε)²)`, where `M₀` bounds the Hessian on the cells of `V̄[U]` and `M ≥ M₀` the finite
Taylor remainder `|h(w) - h(v) - ∇h(v)·(w - v)| ≤ (M/2) ‖w - v‖²` on the internal edges (both
endpoints in `V[U]`); the cells of `V[U]` are complete (finitely many neighbours, boundary covered
by the cells of the neighbours); `h_C` is `C²` on an open set containing the cells of `V̄[U]` and
harmonic on the cells of `V[U]` (the corrected paper asks harmonicity on `Û`, all cells of `V̄[U]`:
a stronger statement).  No local oscillation or Lipschitz condition.  The printed theorem is false
without completeness (check G4 in `GAP-CHECKS.md`: on the square grid of mesh `1/n`, `n` odd, of `D
= [0,1] × [0,2]`, with `U = (0,1) × (1/2, 3/2)` and `h_C = cosh(π(x - 1/2)) cos(π(y - 1))`, the
discrete solution is `0` while `h_C → 1` near the centre, and the printed bound tends to `0`).
Whether the published linear bound holds is not settled here, and whether the theorem holds with the
published cell Hessian constant alone is open.  Proof: the error is split, after leobon12, into a
boundary correction of size at most `2 M₀ ε²` and a corrected error whose energy gives good
rectangles (Lemma 3.1) and which is controlled inside them by the subharmonic comparison with `(M/2)
‖· - v‖²`.

name: theorem33_rate
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
open scoped MeasureTheory Laplacian
doc:
Theorem 3.3 of rw-spheres.tex, the "in particular" clause, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1050-1053` (label `theorem:2d`): in the plane there is
`C = C(U, M, L) < ∞` with `sup_{V[U]} |h_D - h_C| ≤ C ε^{1/2}`, where `ε = sup_{V̄[U]} diam(P_v)`,
`L = sup_Û |∇ h_C|` and `M = sup_Û |∇² h_C|`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4 and 8 and the revised Theorem 3.3,
corrections items 1, 5 and 6): for `0 < ε ≤ 1/2`, `sup_{V[U]} |h_D - h_C| ≤ C ε^{2/3}` (hence `≤ C
ε^{1/2}`), with `C = M (3 + 6 vol(B_{R₀+1}) + (√2 + 1)²/2)`, `R₀` a bound on `‖x‖` over `U`, and `M₀
≤ M` as in the bound (`M₀` the Hessian bound on the cells of `V̄[U]`, `M` the finite Taylor constant
of the internal edges); the cells of `V[U]` are complete (finitely many neighbours, boundary covered
by the cells of the neighbours); `h_C` is `C²` on an open set containing the cells of `V̄[U]` and
harmonic on the cells of `V[U]` (the corrected paper asks harmonicity on `Û`, all cells of `V̄[U]`:
a stronger statement).  The published rate is false with a constant uniform over all meshes: for
large `ε`, a product tiling with a large central cell has an error of order `ε`; the range `ε ≤ 1/2`
is the correction.  The printed theorem is false without completeness (check G4 in `GAP-CHECKS.md`:
on the square grid of mesh `1/n`, `n` odd, of `D = [0,1] × [0,2]`, with `U = (0,1) × (1/2, 3/2)` and
`h_C = cosh(π(x - 1/2)) cos(π(y - 1))`, the discrete solution is `0` while `h_C → 1` near the
centre, and the printed bound tends to `0`).  Whether the rate holds with the published cell Hessian
constant alone is open.  Proof: the bound with `k = ε^{-1/3}`.

opens:

doc:
Lemma 3.5 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1128-1135` (label `lemma:gradient-energy-estimate`):
`∑_{e ∈ E[Ā]} d vol_d(Q_e) 1{|∇f(e)| > δ} ≤ D(f, A)` for every `δ ≥ sup_{e ∈ E[Ā]} ‖e‖`.

leobon12's theorem, for any finite family of edges with lengths at most `δ`, in the form
`d vol_d(Q_e) = ‖e‖ vol_{d-1}(H_e)` (Lemma 2.4).

name: theorem36_rate
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
open scoped MeasureTheory Laplacian
doc:
Theorem 3.6 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1147-1176` (label `theorem:generaldim`): there is `C = C(U)` such
that for `ε < (C M)⁻¹`, `sup_{V[U]} |h_D - h_C| ≤ C M K ε log(1/ε) + D L`, where `ε = sup_{V̄[U]}
diam(P_v)`, `L = sup_Û |∇ h_C|`, `M = sup_Û |∇² h_C| ∨ 1`, `K ≥ 1` is arbitrary, `𝒜 = {v ∈ V̄[U] :
vol_d(P_v) < ε^K}` and `D` is the largest total diameter of a connected component of `𝒜`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4, 8 and 11; Theorem 3.6 with `M =
M_U°(h_C) ∨ 1`): the cells of `V[U]` are complete (finitely many neighbours, boundary covered by the
cells of the neighbours); `h_C` is `C²` on an open set containing the cells of `V̄[U]` and harmonic
on the cells of `V[U]` (the corrected paper asks harmonicity on `Û`, all cells of `V̄[U]`: a
stronger statement); `M ≥ 1` bounds the Hessian on the cells of `V̄[U]` and the finite Taylor
remainder `|h(w) - h(v) - ∇h(v)·(w - v)| ≤ (M/2) ‖w - v‖²` on the internal edges (both endpoints in
`V[U]`); `L` bounds the gradient on the cells of `V̄[U]`; `D` bounds the total diameter of every
connected set of cells of `𝒜`.  The printed theorem is false without completeness (check G4 in
`GAP-CHECKS.md`: on the square grid of mesh `1/n`, `n` odd, of `D = [0,1] × [0,2]`, with `U = (0,1)
× (1/2, 3/2)` and `h_C = cosh(π(x - 1/2)) cos(π(y - 1))`, the discrete solution is `0` while `h_C →
1` near the centre, and the printed bound tends to `0`).  Whether the theorem holds with the
published cell Hessian constant alone is open.  The constant is explicit in `d` and a bound `R₀` on
`‖x‖` over `U`; the smallness condition is `12 M ε ≤ 1` and `ε ≤ 1/2`, an instance of the paper's `ε
< (C M)⁻¹`.  The printed proof has gaps (the exit cell, and estimates on boundary cells that the
iteration does not control); the proof here uses leobon12's corrected iteration, whose boundary-edge
Taylor remainders are bounded by the cell Hessian alone, and on a remaining component `Q` bounds the
error by both `L (D_Q + ε)` and `M ρ²`.

name: prop42_general
opens: open MeasureTheory Metric Filter Set BouRabeeGwynne SpherePackings
doc:
Proposition 4.2 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1511-1516` (label `prop:convergence-of-harmonic-measure`): under
Assumption D, `lim_{n → ∞} sup_{x ∈ B} d_P(hm_n(x), hm(x)) = 0` for the unit ball `B`, where
`hm_n(x)` is the discrete harmonic measure of `∂V_n[B]` seen from `x^n` and `hm(x)` the Brownian
harmonic measure of `∂B` seen from `x`.

Formalized for any sequence of nearest-neighbour walks on graphs in `ℝ^d` (`NearestNeighbourWalk`)
under Assumption D as printed (`AssumptionD`; the existence of the discrete Dirichlet solutions,
which the paper presupposes, is not assumed, and (4.2) is required of every solution), for every ball whose closure lies in
`B_δ(D)`, the set on which Assumption D speaks (the unit ball when its closure lies there).
Correction: the printed statement leaves implicit that the unit ball lies in `B_δ(D)` (its proof
applies (4.2) to the unit ball), and fails without it (a walk that is simple random walk near `D` and moves deterministically near the
unit ball satisfies Assumption D).  `x^n` is the vertex selection of Assumption D, any one
satisfying (4.1).  The uniformity is over the whole open ball.

name: lemma51a_inner
doc:
Lemma 5.1(a) of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1627-1634` (label `lemma:geometric-constraint`): if every cube
`x + [-2r, 2r]^d`, `x ∈ r ℤ^d ∩ U`, contains at most one point of `S`, then `B_r(s) ⊆ 𝒞_s` for every
`s ∈ S ∩ U`.

The statement of the corrected paper (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Correction 15): the condition is
asked of every grid point `x ∈ r ℤ^d` with `(x + [-r, r]^d) ∩ U ≠ ∅`.  The published version is false:
in `ℝ`, `U = (0, 10)`, `r = 1` and `S = {0.1, -1.5}` satisfy its hypothesis, but
`B_1(0.1) ⊄ 𝒞_{0.1} = [-0.7, ∞)` (an informal counterexample).  The conclusion is for the closed ball.

name: lemma51b_outer
doc:
Lemma 5.1(b) of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1635-1641` (label `lemma:geometric-constraint`): there is
`δ = δ(d) ∈ (0, 1)` such that if every cube `y + [-δk, δk]^d`, `y ∈ k ℤ^d ∩ B_{2k}(U)`, contains a
point of `S`, then `𝒞_s ⊆ B_{4k√d}(s)` for every `s ∈ S ∩ U`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Lemma 5.1(b)): there are constants
`δ = δ(d) ∈ (0, 1)` and `R = R(d) ≥ 2` such that, with the grid points of `k ℤ^d ∩ B_{Rk}(U)`, the
same conclusion holds.  Stated here for arbitrary sets `U` and `S` (the paper's bounded domain `U`
and locally finite `S` are not needed).  The proof takes `δ = 1/10` and `R = max(2, 1.1√d)`.  The
published radius `2k` holds for `d ≤ 3` (then `R = 2`) and, with a smaller `δ`, for `4 ≤ d ≤ 12`
(a separate rounding argument, not formalized: there the registered statement is weaker than the
printed one).  It fails for every `d ≥ 13`: with `k = 1`, `s = (-1/100, 1/2, …, 1/2)`,
`U = B_{1/1000}(s)` and `S = {s} ∪ (ℤ^d ∩ B_2(U))`, every tested cube contains a point of `S` for
every `δ > 0`, while `s + 5√d e₁ ∈ 𝒞_s`.

name: lemma52_dual_polytope
doc:
Lemma 5.2 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1650-1653` (label `lemma:dual-polytope-bound`): there is
`δ'(d) ∈ (0, 1)` such that for all `x^{(i±)} ∈ [-δ', δ']^d ± e_i`, the polar
`P* = {y : x ⬝ y ≤ 1 ∀ x ∈ P}` of `P = conv(x^{(1+)}, x^{(1-)}, …, x^{(d+)}, x^{(d-)})` lies in
`B_{2√d}`.  As printed, for `d ≥ 1`.

name: theorem61_counterexample
opens:
open MeasureTheory Metric Filter Set BouRabeeGwynne SpherePackings
open scoped ENNReal Topology
doc:
Theorem 6.1 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1791-1794` (label `theorem:counter-example`): for all `d ≥ 3` there
is a sphere packing of `ℝ^d` on which simple random walk with unit conductance does not converge to
Brownian motion modulo time parametrization in the scaling limit; the radii are `1` or `1/2` and
each sphere is tangent to a bounded number of others.

"Does not converge" is formalized for the walk started at the centre `0`, positions scaled by `1/n`,
stopped on leaving the unit ball: these laws exist and do not converge to the law of Brownian motion
from `0` stopped on leaving the unit ball, in the Lévy–Prokhorov distance for curves modulo time
parametrization.  In dimension three the packing is the printed one, and every sphere is covered
(`rw-spheres.tex:331-333`: the hyperplanes tangent to it at its contact points bound a bounded
polytope).  For `d ≥ 4` the packing differs
from the printed one (small spheres at even coordinates beyond the third), for which the printed
hitting computation fails; this packing does not cover `ℝ^d` (a small sphere other than the middle
ones touches others only in the first three coordinate directions).  The statement, like the
printed one, does not ask that the packing cover `ℝ^d`.

name: lemma25_dual_coverage
doc:
Lemma 2.5 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:769-784` (label `lemma:easy-global-qe-bounds`): for every bounded
`U ⊆ D`, `U ⊆ ⋃_{e ∈ E[Ū]} Q_e ⊆ Ĝ_U`.

The statement of the corrected paper (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4 and 7): when the
cells of `V[U]` are complete (finitely many neighbours, and every boundary point of the cell lies in
the cell of a neighbour), `⋃_{v ∈ V[U]} P_v ⊆ ⋃_{e ∈ E[Ū]} Q_e ⊆ Ĝ_U`.  The published first inclusion
is false (informal counterexample: a small ball inside one square of the unit grid contains no
vertex, so the union is empty), and without completeness the cells need not be covered (two unit
squares).  The second inclusion holds as printed.  Proved from leobon12's cell pyramids.

name: prop26_energy
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
open scoped MeasureTheory Laplacian
doc:
Proposition 2.6 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:822-844` (label `prop:energy-bound`):
`D(h_D - h_C, U) ≤ 9 M² ε² ∑_{e ∈ E[Ū]} d vol_d(Q_e)`, with `ε = sup_{V̄[U]} diam(P_v)` and
`M = sup_{Û} |∇² h_C|`, for `h_C ∈ C²(Û)` harmonic on `Û`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4 and 8): the cells of `V[U]` are
complete; `h_C` is `C²` on an open set containing the cells of `V̄[U]` and harmonic on the cells of
`V[U]`; `M` bounds the Hessian on the cells of `V[U]` and, for each edge of `E[Ū]`, the finite
Taylor remainder at one active endpoint, `|h(w) - h(v) - ∇h(v)·(w - v)| ≤ (M/2) ‖w - v‖²`
(harmonicity and the Hessian bound are asked only on the cells of `V[U]`, not on all cells of
`V̄[U]` as in the corrected paper: a stronger statement).  The
published version is false: without completeness (two unit squares, energy `2`, right side `0`),
and, with complete cells, for a slit-domain harmonic function (the Hessian bound on the cells does
not control the edge segments that leave `Û`; check G2 in `GAP-CHECKS.md`).  A Hessian bound `M`
on the edge segments implies the Taylor condition.  `incidentEnergy` and `incidentMass` sum over
undirected edges, each half the printed directed sum, so the constant `9` is unchanged.  Proved
from leobon12's flux-residual bounds.

name: prop32_columns
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
open scoped MeasureTheory Laplacian
doc:
Proposition 3.2 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:980-1001` (label `prop:energy-poincare-bound`): the
`(d-1)`-volume of the set of `y ∈ π_j(U)` with
`max_{v ∈ L_y^j[U]} |h_D(v) - h_C(v)| > 3 k M ε ∑_{e ∈ E[Ū]} d vol_d(Q_e)` is at most `1/k`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4 and 8), with the hypotheses of the
corrected Proposition 2.6: complete cells of `V[U]`, and `M` bounding the Hessian on the cells of
`V[U]` and the finite Taylor remainder at one active endpoint of each edge of `E[Ū]` (harmonicity
and the Hessian bound only on the cells of `V[U]`: stronger than the corrected paper).  The
published version is false: without completeness (two unit squares, `U` a small disk around the
centre of one and `h_C(x) = x₁`: `M = 0` while the error at that centre is `1`), and, with complete
cells, for a thin reflected Voronoi configuration in which the Hessian bound on `Û` alone does not
control the edge segments.  Columns in any direction `e ≠ 0`, the bad set being the set of `y` in
the projection of the cell of a vertex of `V[U]` where the error exceeds the threshold.
`incidentMass` is the undirected sum, half the printed one, so the threshold is half the printed one
(stronger).  Proved from leobon12's column lemmas, adapted to complete cells.

name: theorem41
opens:
open MeasureTheory Metric Filter Set BouRabeeGwynne SpherePackings
open scoped ENNReal Topology
doc:
Theorem 4.1 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1481-1488` (label `theorem:general-clt`): if Assumption D holds and
`U ⊆ D` is a bounded Lipschitz domain, the supremum over `z ∈ U` of the Prokhorov distance between
the laws of the walk from `z^n`, interpolated and stopped at its first exit from `V_n[U]`, and of
Brownian motion from `z` stopped at its exit from `U`, in the metric (1.2), tends to `0`.

Formalized for any sequence of nearest-neighbour walks on graphs with vertices in `ℝ^d`
(`NearestNeighbourWalk`: a Markov kernel on the vertex set whose steps follow the edges of an
undirected graph) under Assumption D as printed (`AssumptionD`; the existence of the discrete Dirichlet solutions,
which the paper presupposes, is not assumed, and (4.2) is required of every solution).  `z^n` is any nearest
vertex of `z` (the paper breaks ties lexicographically).  The laws are on curves modulo time
parametrization with the metric (1.2), the distance is Lévy–Prokhorov, and the walk is also shown
to leave `V_n[U]` almost surely for large `n`.  The proof adapts leobon12's coupling from his
proof of Theorem A to an arbitrary kernel.

name: theorem37_rate
opens:
open BouRabeeGwynne BouRabeeGwynne.OrthogonalTiling SpherePackings
open scoped ENNReal MeasureTheory Laplacian
doc:
Theorem 3.7 of rw-spheres.tex, frozen.

Paper statement, `rw-spheres.tex:1314-1340` (label `theorem:generaldim-decay`): under
`diam(P_v) ≤ F sup_{e = (w, v)} vol_d(Q_e)^α` for `v ∈ V[U]`, there is `C = C(U, F, α)` such that
for `ε < (C M)⁻¹`, `sup_{V[U]} |h_D - h_C| ≤ C M ε log(1/ε)`, with `ε = sup_{V̄[U]} diam(P_v)` and
`M = sup_Û |∇² h_C| ∨ 1`.

Corrected statement (`rw-spheres-corrected.tex`, Corrections 4, 8 and 11; Theorem 3.7 with `M =
M_U°(h_C) ∨ 1`): the cells of `V[U]` are complete (finitely many neighbours, boundary covered by the
cells of the neighbours); `h_C` is `C²` on an open set containing the cells of `V̄[U]` and harmonic
on the cells of `V[U]` (the corrected paper asks harmonicity on `Û`, all cells of `V̄[U]`: a
stronger statement); `M ≥ 1` bounds the Hessian on the cells of `V̄[U]` and the finite Taylor
remainder `|h(w) - h(v) - ∇h(v)·(w - v)| ≤ (M/2) ‖w - v‖²` on the internal edges (both endpoints in
`V[U]`).  The printed theorem is false without completeness (check G4 in `GAP-CHECKS.md`: on the
square grid of mesh `1/n`, `n` odd, of `D = [0,1] × [0,2]`, with `U = (0,1) × (1/2, 3/2)` and `h_C =
cosh(π(x - 1/2)) cos(π(y - 1))`, the discrete solution is `0` while `h_C → 1` near the centre, and
the printed bound tends to `0`).  Whether the theorem holds with the published cell Hessian constant
alone is open.  The rate has an explicit constant (`hypIIIRateConstant`, in `d`, `F`, `α` and a
bound `R₀` on `‖x‖` over `U`); the smallness condition is `12 M ε ≤ 1` and `ε ≤ 1/2`, an instance of
the paper's `ε < (C M)⁻¹`.  The printed proof has a gap at `rw-spheres.tex:1371` (check G1,
`GAP-CHECKS.md`); the proof here uses leobon12's corrected iteration, whose boundary-edge Taylor
remainders are bounded by the cell Hessian alone.  The decay hypothesis is in leobon12's form
`diam(P_v) ≤ F sup_w (‖w - v‖ vol_{d-1}(P_v ∩ P_w))^α`, equivalent to the printed one by Lemma 2.4
(`F` scaled by `d^α`).
